name: Why Don't You Get A Job

podcast.body: This song was featured on the 1998 Americana album, contributing to its signature blend of pop punk fun. "Offsprings Americana album was full of pop punk fun like this, along with songs like Why Don't You Get A Job."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released as a single in March 1999 from their "Americana" album. It was noted for sounding "an awful lot like" The Beatles' "Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da," which had been released 31 years earlier on "The White Album." As far as is known, no public action was taken, and the similarity was treated as a form of homage. "The offspring with Why Don't You Get A Job, which sounds an awful lot like the Beatles Uble Diobla Duh."

podcast.body: The song from 1998 by The Offspring implicitly introduces the theme of people with multiple occupations, highlighting the non-musical pursuits of its lead singer, Dexter Holland. "The offspring from 1998 with why don't you get a job?"

podcast.body: Released in March 1999 as a single from their *Americana* album, this song bears a strong resemblance to The Beatles' "Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da," which was released 31 years prior on *The White Album*. Despite the sonic similarities, no public legal action was initiated, and the resemblance was reportedly regarded as "some kind of homage." "The offspring with Why Don't You Get A Job, which sounds an awful lot like the Beatles Uble Diobla Duh, which was released on the white album of 31 years earlier."
